anachnid.bio:
Montréal-based Anachnid is an Oji-Cree and Mi'kmaq multidisciplinary artist whose electronic music, visual identity and storytelling draw directly from Indigenous experience without reducing it to a single genre or message. Raised largely in Atikamekw territory in western Québec, she developed a performance language that moves between experimental pop, electronic production and Indigenous cultural reference. Her early singles, including "Windigo" and "Sky Woman," introduced an artist comfortable turning traditional stories, contemporary urban life and personal mythology into the same sonic world.

Her 2020 debut album Dreamweaver brought that work to a wider Canadian audience. The album was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize and earned Félix nominations, while Anachnid's songwriting and performance work also received recognition from the Indigenous Music Awards. In 2021, she won the Félix for Indigenous Artist of the Year, confirming her as one of the more distinctive Indigenous voices in Québec's contemporary music scene. Songs from Dreamweaver balance atmospheric electronic production with direct writing about identity, violence, spirituality and survival, making the record feel both personal and politically aware without becoming didactic.

Anachnid's significance lies in how naturally she connects scenes that are often kept separate: Indigenous music, Montréal experimental pop and electronic production. Rather than presenting tradition and modernity as opposites, her work treats them as part of the same living identity. Later releases including "Freak of Nature" and 2026's "Happy Birthday" have kept that approach active, while her broader multidisciplinary practice reinforces the sense that Anachnid is building a world around the music rather than simply a catalogue of songs.
anachnid.directory_summary: Montréal-based Oji-Cree and Mi'kmaq artist Anachnid blends experimental pop, electronic production and Indigenous storytelling into a highly distinctive multidisciplinary practice. Her 2020 debut Dreamweaver was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize and helped lead to a 2021 Félix for Indigenous Artist of the Year. Songs such as "Windigo" and "Sky Woman" place spirituality, identity and contemporary urban Indigenous experience inside a modern electronic framework, making her an important bridge between Québec's alternative scene and a wider Indigenous music movement.

löv.bio:
LÖV is a Cree R&B and soul singer-songwriter from Treaty 6 Territory whose music is built around resilience, self-definition and matriarchal strength. Her work draws from UK-influenced soul and contemporary R&B, but the emotional centre is intensely personal: songs about independence, family, healing and the decision to reclaim control of her own story. That focus has made LÖV's rise feel less like a conventional debut campaign than a deliberate artistic reset, with each release strengthening a persona grounded in both vulnerability and authority.

A creative partnership with Montréal producer Connor Seidel helped sharpen that sound into a polished, spacious form where LÖV's smoky vocals remain the main event. Early singles including "Mama," "Matriarch," "Relate" and "Sister Era" built substantial streaming momentum, while "Mama" reached No. 1 on the Indigenous Music Countdown. Her music has also appeared on major Spotify and Apple Music editorial playlists, and coverage from CBC and APTN has helped expand her profile beyond western Canada.

By 2025 and 2026, LÖV's presence was extending beyond recordings into fashion, live performance and artist-development spaces, including Native Fashion Week and a Massey Hall artist-in-residence program. Her debut project Iskwêw gives that growth a clear frame: contemporary soul built around Indigenous womanhood, family and autonomy without treating any of those subjects as marketing categories. Within Northern Dial's Indigenous coverage, LÖV represents the R&B side of a broader movement in which Indigenous artists are defining modern pop and soul on their own terms.
löv.directory_summary: Treaty 6 Cree singer-songwriter LÖV brings a smoky, UK-influenced soul voice to contemporary Indigenous R&B. Singles including "Mama," "Matriarch" and "Sister Era" centre family, resilience and self-definition, with "Mama" reaching No. 1 on the Indigenous Music Countdown. Working with producer Connor Seidel, she has developed a polished but emotionally direct sound that places Indigenous womanhood and matriarchal strength inside modern soul rather than treating them as separate themes.

felix cartal.bio:
Vancouver producer Felix Cartal began in the harder edge of the late-2000s electro-house boom before gradually developing into one of Canada's most reliable melodic dance-pop producers. Born Taelor Deitcher, he came out of a punk background and signed with Steve Aoki's Dim Mak label, releasing Popular Music in 2010 and Different Faces in 2012. Those records established him internationally as part of the festival-era electronic scene, but they also set up a longer evolution away from distortion-heavy club music toward more song-driven production.

That shift became especially clear on 2018's Next Season, where Cartal leaned into melodic house, pop structures and emotionally direct vocal collaborations. His work with Canadian singer Lights on "Love Me" became a major domestic success and won the 2020 JUNO for Dance Recording of the Year. The Sophie Simmons collaboration "Mine" also reached platinum status in Canada, while Expensive Sounds for Nice People gathered those singles into a fuller statement of his second-act sound. The album paired dance production with singers including Kiiara, KROY and Karen Harding and showed how far Cartal had moved from his early electro identity.

Cartal's career matters because it spans several distinct eras of Canadian electronic music without being trapped in any of them. He moved from blog-era electro to polished streaming-era house while retaining a recognizable preference for strong hooks and vocal songwriting. Later work, including 2025's I, Sabotage, extended that trajectory rather than simply revisiting past formulas, making Felix Cartal a useful link between Canada's early EDM export wave and a more mature, pop-oriented electronic scene.
felix cartal.directory_summary: Vancouver producer Felix Cartal has evolved from late-2000s electro-house into one of Canada's most durable melodic dance-pop artists. Early albums Popular Music and Different Faces established his festival-era credentials, while Next Season and Expensive Sounds for Nice People shifted toward vocal-driven house. His Lights collaboration "Love Me" won the 2020 JUNO for Dance Recording of the Year, and later platinum singles reinforced a career built on adapting across multiple electronic-music eras without losing a strong pop songwriting instinct.

haley smalls.bio:
Toronto-born Haley Smalls has built one of the more sustained independent R&B catalogues in Canada by combining expressive vocals, candid songwriting and unusually hands-on control over her recordings. Classically trained as a singer, she was recording in professional studios from a young age and later taught herself audio engineering, a skill that became central to her independence. Rather than separating performance from production, Smalls developed as an artist, songwriter and engineer at the same time, giving her work a consistency that has survived multiple changes in the R&B landscape.

Her first major run of projects began with the 2015 mixtapes This Is Me and Imagination and continued through The Cure, The Cure II, Heart of Gold and 2019's Summer Nights. Longtime collaborator Megaman helped shape a sound that balances contemporary R&B polish with a softer, more intimate vocal approach. A 2014 moment in which Beyoncé shared Smalls' cover of "Pretty Hurts" brought a burst of international attention, but Smalls ultimately doubled down on an independent path instead of treating that exposure as a route into the label system.

That long-game approach has continued through later releases including The Cure III, Timelines, 333, The Cure IV and 2025's Matches. By 2026, Smalls was touring internationally while maintaining the direct-to-fan model that had defined her career. Her significance in Canadian R&B comes less from one crossover hit than from durability and control: she has built a sizeable catalogue, developed technical authority over her own sound and shown how an independent Toronto artist can sustain audience growth without relying on a single industry breakthrough.
haley smalls.directory_summary: Toronto R&B singer, songwriter and recording engineer Haley Smalls has built a long-running independent catalogue around expressive vocals and unusually strong creative control. Beginning with 2015's This Is Me and Imagination, she developed through projects including The Cure series, Summer Nights, Timelines and 2025's Matches. A 2014 Beyoncé co-sign brought early international attention, but Smalls' lasting story is independence: she taught herself engineering, built a durable partnership with producer Megaman and turned steady releases into an increasingly global audience.

puma june.bio:
Toronto-based Puma June is a multi-instrumentalist, vocalist, songwriter and producer whose alt-R&B sound pulls from pop, jazz and hip-hop while treating visual presentation as part of the same creative practice. A classically trained violinist who grew up in and around Barrie, Ontario, she later studied independent music production at Seneca College. That technical background helped her approach songwriting and production as interconnected disciplines rather than separate roles, while a feminist perspective became a recurring frame for songs about autonomy, desire and the expectations placed on women.

Momentum accelerated through 2024 as Puma June received the RBCxMusic and Prism Prize MVP Project Grant, joined the RBCxMusic First Up program and was selected for the SOCAN Foundation's EquityXProduction initiative. Her video for "My Body, My Problem" was also selected for the Canadian showcase at the Toronto International Music Video Festival, reinforcing the importance of image and multidisciplinary presentation to her work. Those development opportunities fed directly into her debut EP A Woman That They Want, released in March 2025.

By 2026, Puma June was moving from emerging-artist programs into larger showcase stages, including JUNOfest, Departure Festival and Billboard Canada Live at NXNE. Her importance is still being written, but the trajectory is already clear: she represents a generation of Canadian independent artists who are expected to write, perform, produce and build a visual world around their work at the same time. In alt-R&B specifically, that combination gives Puma June a distinct identity rather than simply placing her inside an existing Toronto sound.
puma june.directory_summary: Toronto-based Puma June is a classically trained violinist, singer, songwriter and producer building a cinematic alt-R&B sound from pop, jazz and hip-hop influences. After studying independent music production at Seneca, she earned support from RBCxMusic, the Prism Prize and the SOCAN Foundation before releasing her debut EP A Woman That They Want in 2025. Her work pairs feminist songwriting with a strong visual practice, making her a notable example of the increasingly multidisciplinary approach shaping Canada's next generation of independent R&B artists.
